verdict.rationale: Meilisearch documents its own scoped credentials. Tenant tokens are short-lived, scoped credentials derived from an API key, and they embed filters that restrict what data each request can see; API keys authenticate requests. The evidence only covers search-level data scoping, though. It does not document per-action or per-index permissions on API keys, or how scoped credentials apply to an agent using the MCP route. Missing for 10: documented action- and index-level API key permissions, agent- or MCP-specific credential scoping guidance, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Tenant tokens are short-lived, scoped credentials generated from an API key. They embed search rules (filters) that automatically apply to every search request, ensuring users only see their own data.
Meilisearch uses API keys and tenant tokens to control access to your data.
API keys authenticate requests, while tenant tokens restrict what data each user can see within a shared index.
